title: A readability score is not difficulty
statement: A readability score is not a text's difficulty: judge difficulty from the exact excerpt students read, by reading it as well as by formula.
detail: The staged assessment standard flags a readability score as a secondary proxy, not item difficulty itself (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/pr-proposals/ti-courseplans-standards/staged/docs/standards/assessment-design.md`). The project's reading-science summary holds that text difficulty is a match among the text, the reader's knowledge and the task, so no single readability number can gate a text (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/applied/teaching-comprehension-insights-brainlift.qmd`). Its digest of a national reading study records that readability estimates disagree with one another and give no diagnostic information for individualizing instruction (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/skills/reading-science/DIGEST-rand-mr1465-2002.qmd`; RAND Reading Study Group 2002, https://www.rand.org/pubs/monograph_reports/MR1465.html). Weigh the new knowledge the excerpt carries, the reader's knowledge and the task. Rate decoding and understanding separately, gate no text on one number, and never swap out the words that carry its knowledge to lower a score.
against: The measure is a heuristic: the notes call the FK-to-band reading "a judgment call, not a psychometric fact" and say the bands are not to be reused as policy (the same file, lines 4 and 15). For that same book, a documented whole-book Lexile measure was kept as the better evidence of its band, ahead of the formula's own figures (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/pd-texts/winnie-the-pooh-onepager.md`, line 27).
